edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), De baptismo, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Est quidem nobis etiam secundum lavacrum, unum et ipsum, sanguinis scilicet: de quo Dominus: Habeo, inquit, Baptismo tingui, cum jam tinctus fuisset. Venerat enim per aquam et sanguinem, sicut Joannes scripsit, ut aqua tingueretur, sanguine glorificaretur, proinde nos faceret aqua vocatos, sanguine electos. Hos duos baptismos de vulnere perfossi lateris emisit, quia qui in sanguinem ejus crederent, aqua lavarentur: qui aqua lavissent, etiam sanguinem potarent. Hic est Baptismus, qui lavacrum et non acceptum repraesentat, et perditum reddit.
pass_a_gloss: There is indeed for us also a second washing, one and the same, namely of blood: concerning which the Lord says: I have, He says, to be baptized with a baptism, when He had already been baptized. For He came through water and blood, as John wrote, so that He might be baptized with water, glorified with blood, and thus make us called with water, chosen with blood. He sent forth these two baptisms from the wound of His pierced side, because those who would believe in His blood would be washed with water: those who would be washed with water would also drink His blood. This is the Baptism which represents a washing not accepted and renders it lost.

choices.why: literal translation of first person singular of habeo

pass_b_english: We also have a second washing, one and the same thing: the washing of blood. The Lord speaks of it: 'I have a baptism to be baptized with,' He says, even though He had already been baptized (Luke 12:50). He came through water and blood, just as John wrote, so that He might be baptized with water, glorified with blood, and thus make us called by water, chosen by blood (John 19:34-35; 1 John 5:6). He poured out these two baptisms from the wound in His pierced side, so that those who believe in His blood would be washed with water, and those who have been washed with water would also drink His blood. This is the Baptism that represents a washing not accepted and renders it lost.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Scripture citations added in Pass B (Luke 12:50, John 19:34-35, 1 John 5:6) correctly identify the biblical allusions present in the Latin text.
